title: The Doorframe: three pencil marks to the tape
hook: How many hikes until variable costs more?
hookAlts: [Exact-number cold open] Variable starts $150 a month cheaper than fixed.
[Mark the date] December 9 could draw the first pencil mark.
mechanic: Guess-then-reveal plus countdown: slide 1 asks for a pick (1, 2, 3 or 4, answer on slide 6) and slide 2 repeats it for people who land there first; each swipe adds one pencil mark and shrinks the gap ($150, $96, $41); the tape crossing every slide edge and the pencil on slide 5 are the swipe cues. The uninsured note on slide 6 makes '4' a right answer too, which gives guessers a reason to comment.

cover: Slide 1 is the grid cover. Cover line: 'How many hikes until variable costs more?' with kicker 'Fixed or variable at renewal'. Every word inside x 60-1020 so the 3:4 profile crop (x 34-1046) keeps it; tape and the single low mark must read at 260 px wide. No logo.
caption:
Fixed or variable at renewal: it takes three quarter-point hikes before variable costs more than fixed (insured rates, Nov 18).
Amit Khurana, Mortgage Agent Level 2 · Lic. M12000871 · Centum Indigo Mortgages Corp. · Brokerage Lic. #12141

Illustrative Mississauga renewal: $420,000 left on a 20-year amortization. The insured 5-year fixed at 4.34% works out to about $2,612 a month. Variable at 3.65% (prime 4.70% minus 1.05%) is about $2,462, so variable starts $150 a month lower.

Each 0.25% hike adds about $54 a month on this mortgage. After two hikes variable is still $41 cheaper. The third takes it to $2,626, past fixed.

The Bank of Canada raised its rate on Oct 28 and decides again on Dec 9. Fixed rates follow bond yields, so they can move before then too.

Over five years of interest: if rates hold, about $69,300 on variable. One hike that sticks, about $74,100. Three hikes in the first six months, about $83,100. Fixed, about $82,800. If rates fall, variable gets cheaper still. Fixed gives you a payment that can't move, which may suit a tight budget.

Uninsured renewals are priced higher and the gap is wider. nesto showed 4.95% fixed and 4.10% variable on Nov 19, a 0.85-point gap, so it takes four hikes.

Your own number: take the fixed and variable rates on your renewal offer, subtract, divide by 0.25 and round up.

Send this to whoever signs the renewal with you.

Illustrative, not an offer. Insured 5-year rates advertised on Ratehub, Nov 18, 2026 (variable = prime 4.70% minus 1.05%); uninsured rates from nesto, Nov 19, 2026. 5-year term, APR [to be confirmed by the brokerage]. $420,000 balance, 20-year amortization, adjustable-payment variable with the payment re-set at each change, semi-annual compounding, each hike assumed to pass through in full. 2021 example: $500,000 at 2.09%, 25 years. Rates change daily and depend on your situation; subject to approval.

sendTest: One partner forwards it to the other the week the renewal letter arrives, with 'it takes three hikes, let's look before we sign.' Second path: a GTA homeowner sends it to a sibling or friend who renewed variable this year and keeps asking whether to lock in.

whyThisClient: Amit's site lists refinance and renewal as a specialty and he serves Mississauga and the GTA, where the pandemic-era 5-year fixed renewal wave lands hardest (BoC FSR). The Oct 28 hike made 'should I lock in' a top Canadian search this week, and most renewal posts either predict Dec 9 or show two rates side by side. This one gives a GTA renewer a count they can check against their own offer, and the uninsured note fits how many GTA owners actually renew. The doorframe device is unused in the radar and the library.
complianceNotes: Ontario O. Reg. 188/08 s.6: the kit footer shows Amit's name, title and both licence numbers but not the brokerage name, so the verbatim complianceLine text goes above the footer on all 8 slides (>= 20 px) and in caption line 2.

O. Reg. 191/08 s.18: the rates are third-party market references (Ratehub, nesto), labelled 'market reference, not an offer' with the 5-year term. APR placeholder kept visible on slide 7 and in the caption until the broker of record confirms wording; do not post with the TODO tag.
No 'lowest' or 'best rate' wording anywhere, including source lines (rephrased to 'advertised on Ratehub').
No Dec 9 odds on screen or in the caption (single-tracker figure); both outcomes shown on slide 4.
Fixed rates are described as following bond yields; the Bank of Canada is never said to move fixed rates.
Every number labelled illustrative; payment type (adjustable-payment variable) and compounding stated; story mortgage is a labelled composite, no real client.
Rate premise expires on Dec 9 (the decision changes prime either way): re-render with new rates or retire after Dec 9; hard review Dec 18 (30 days).
Carousel, no voiceover: no AI label needed. Add a Meta Sound Collection track when posting (no licensed songs).
needs: APR wording from the broker of record for third-party rate references (slide 7 and caption tag).
A headshot of at least 600 px on the short side if the planned 'Amit beside the frame' slide 8 is wanted; kit photo.png is 305x188, so slide 8 uses the footer portrait only.
Brokerage name check: kit/logo say 'Centum Indigo Mortgages Corp.', the website says 'CENTUM Indigo Mortgage Corp.'; the compliance line uses the kit/logo/licence form.
Brand colours are provisional (website-derived navy #003047, burgundy #8F022A).
Re-check Ratehub and nesto rates on render day; if the gap moves past 0.75 the insured answer becomes 4 and slides 5-8 change.
